subject: Acceptance Surge & Close Velocity Insurance — MAP updates and risk ledger
messages:
From: Carol Hanson <carol@atlasai.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-12-14T09:02:00-08:00
Subject: Re: MAP alignment — acceptance risk

Marissa —

Thanks for the sync yesterday. We ran the org-level review with our engineering and procurement leads overnight. Two items to call out that change our close runway:

1) Acceptance window: our security team wants an extra 2 weeks of ASV testing after the evaluation gate. That pushes our acceptance milestone by ~10 business days.
2) Procurement hold: we have an internal budget sign-off that cannot be completed until the legal redlines land (they expect a PO request buildout).

I attached the initial risk ledger that our PM compiled (risk_log_v1.xlsx). Would appreciate Redwood's view on whether we can provide an "acceptance surge" path (a short canary + extended verification period) so we don't lose the December go-live window entirely.

Carol
Director, Platform Partnerships
Atlas AI
Attachment: risk_log_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet, 120KB)
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Carol Hanson <carol@atlasai.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-12-14T10:10:00-08:00
Subject: Re: MAP alignment — acceptance risk

Carol — thanks for the heads up and for the ledger. Short summary of what we can offer and a proposed MAP tweak: 

- Acceptance Surge (what I mean by "velocity insurance"): we can schedule a two-week canary in a Dedicated pool with a fixed token-capacity reservation. During the canary we run your ASV tests against a customer-scoped environment; if critical issues surface we pause cutover and fall back to the hosted variant.
- Extended verification: we can accept a longer verification window without charging additional platform setup fees if Atlas commits to the canary reservation and a 30-day post-acceptance monitoring SLA.
- Procurement workaround: we can provide a lightweight SOW summary and a standard PO template that legal can plug into the redlines to accelerate sign-off.

Actionable next steps: 
1) I'll upload an updated MAP (MAP-v2.pdf) with the canary timeline and the linked acceptance checks (service, perf, ASV pass/fail).
2) Karthik, can you confirm whether we can hold the Dedicated pool reservation for two weeks in week-of Dec 20 if Atlas signs the PO draft by end of next week?
3) Carol, can you confirm the exact ASV checklist items so we can map them to the canary tests?

Thanks — attaching the MAP draft for discussion.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Sr. Manager, Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference
Attachment: MAP-v2.pdf (PDF, 350KB)
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Carol Hanson <carol@atlasai.com>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-12-14T13:35:00-08:00
Subject: Re: MAP alignment — acceptance risk

Marissa/Carol —

We can reserve a 2-week Dedicated slot w/ reserved capacity, but procurement has one ask: Atlas needs to approve a credit hold or a pre-authorized charge instrument for the reservation. If procurement can't approve a PO before Dec 20 we risk losing the reservation window (capacity is limited over year-end).

I'm attaching a short note that procurement suggested to their counterpart (procurement_hold_notes.txt). If Atlas can accept a credit hold OR confirm the PO submission timeline we can mark the reservation as "soft-held" until Dec 18. After that it becomes first-come-first-served.

Also, quick technical note on the canary plan: ensure tests include KV-cache warmup and a burst profile run (we saw a regression on a different account recently when burst > 1.5x normal traffic). That will be in MAP-v2 test matrix.

—Karthik
Director, Strategic Sales Operations
Attachment: procurement_hold_notes.txt (plain text, 4KB)
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Carol Hanson <carol@atlasai.com>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-12-15T08:20:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Acceptance Surge & Close Velocity Insurance — MAP updates and risk ledger

Team — 

Thanks for moving quickly here. Two things from an escalation/exec-readiness perspective: 

1) Exec brief: Marissa, can you prepare a one-pager for Atlas execs that summarizes the tradeoffs (canary benefits, acceptance window extension, procurement contingency) and the exact fallback triggers (ASV fail -> pause; performance > 1.8x burst -> rollback)? We'll need that to get buy-in from our CSM and solutions execs.
2) Runbook stub: Naomi, please draft a minimal rollback/runbook that covers immediate mitigation steps if a canary fails (disable canary routing, revert to hosted model, open incident and notify Atlas SRE). Keep it short — this will be appended to the MAP as the "insurance" section.

If both bullets are ready by EOD Dec 15 we can present to Atlas execs on Dec 16 and lock the PO path. Otherwise we'll need to consider a compressed timeline into Jan.

Jonas
VP, Sales Strategy
From: Carol Hanson <carol@atlasai.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Raj Patel <raj.patel@soltiva.com>, procurement@atlasai.com
Date: 2027-12-15T16:45:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Acceptance Surge & Close Velocity Insurance — MAP updates and risk ledger

Marissa/Jonas —

Appreciate the rapid replies. Quick status: procurement greenlit the PO draft contingent on the MAP and the runbook language. Raj confirmed a verbal ok and will push the PO through by Dec 17 EOD if we include the rollback triggers and the ASV test matrix in the MAP.

We're good to proceed with the canary/reservation path. Please include the following in the MAP-v2 final: 
- explicit ASV checklist (items 1-6)
- rollback criteria phrased as "hard stop" conditions
- a 30-day post-acceptance monitoring window and a single incident-credit clause

If you can circulate the one-pager and the runbook as attachments by morning Dec 16 we'll route internally and confirm the PO. Thanks for the "velocity insurance" framing — that made it easier to sell internally.

Carol
Director, Platform Partnerships
Atlas AI

Thread notes: MAP-v2.pdf was iterated and uploaded to Drive (link above). Internal action items: Marissa to draft exec one-pager; Naomi to prepare runbook stub; Karthik to soft-hold reserve until Dec 18 pending PO. Procurement and acceptance items captured in risk_log_v1.xlsx.
